extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, authorized representatives, and IP office staff in ARIPO member states
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, formal and substantive examination criteria, and procedural steps for filing, prosecuting, and obtaining patents, utility models and industrial designs under the Harare Protocol administered by ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harare Protocol authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Harare Protocol empowered ARIPO to grant patents and to register utility models and industrial designs and to administer such patents, utility models and industrial designs on behalf of Contracting States in accordance with the provisions of the Harare Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARIPO grants and registers rights that in each designated Contracting State have the effect of, and are subject to the same conditions as, a national patent/utility model/industrial design of that State (Sec. 1(1), Sec. 2(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Duration of rights under the Harare Protocol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents — 20 years; Industrial Designs — 10 years; Utility Models — 10 years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons/entities entitled to file ARIPO applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants: individuals from Contracting States and private or public entities; applications may be filed by an authorized representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where and how to file
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted filing offices and modes of filing for ARIPO applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where to file: National IP Offices (receiving offices) or directly to ARIPO. Modes: post, e-mail, fax, courier, depositing at ARIPO, online filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content — patents and utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum contents required in a patent or utility model application (Sec. 3(1); 3ter(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must include: a request identifying the applicant (Form 3+); a description of the invention; one or more claim(s); drawings/sequence listing when necessary; an abstract; designation of contracting State(s); payment of prescribed fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements for filing date allocation — patents/utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents required to obtain a filing date for patents and utility models (Rule 14/Rule 9).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) a request Form (Form 3); 2) a description; 3) one or more claims. If met, a filing date notification (Form 12 or 33) is issued; if not, applicant is invited (Form 11 or 32) to comply within 2 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum requirements for filing date allocation — industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents required to obtain a filing date for industrial designs (Rule 14 & Rule 10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) a request Form (Form 28); 2) a reproduction of the industrial designs; 3) a designation of at least one state. Same filing-date issuance/invitation consequences as patents/UMs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Formality requirements that must be satisfied during formality examination (S.3(1); S.3ter(3); S.4(1); R.5-8, R.10, R11; Rule 15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: request Form (Form 3); description; one or more claims; drawing(s)/sequence listing when necessary; abstract; designation of at least one state; English translation if filed in another language; payment of application and designation fees or an undertaking to pay within 21 days; acceptable physical document requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to comply when filing date requirements not met
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure if minimum filing-date requirements are not satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant is invited (Form 11 or 32) to comply within 2 months to secure the filing date; failure to comply triggers usual procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination — request requirement (post-2017)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination is undertaken only after formality requirements are met and, for applications filed from 1 January 2017, on request by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must submit Form 13A to request substantive examination for patent applications filed from 1 Jan 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and examination report obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: A search and examination report shall be established containing the conclusions of the substantive examination (R.18(2)-Patent/R.18ter-Utility Model).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports accompany Form 18/Form 21 notifications and summarize examination findings and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of subject matter that are not patentable (Sec.3(10)h-j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include discoveries, scientific theories, mathematical methods, methods of treatment, plant or animal varieties, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear and complete disclosure (enablement)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application must disclose the invention sufficiently clear and complete for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art (Sec. 2bis(1)(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description must enable a skilled person to reproduce/perform the invention; insufficient disclosure is ground for objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and full support of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define the matter for which protection is sought and be clear, concise and supported by the description (Sec. 2bis(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims lacking clarity or adequate support in the description can be objected to during substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: An ARIPO patent application shall relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept (Sec. 2bis(1)(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity exists only when there is a technical relationship among the claimed inventions involving one or more of the same or corresponding special technical features. 'Special technical features' are those that make a contribution over the prior art and are present in each claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability criteria — overview
rubrics_metrics.description: General patentability requirements under Sec. 3(10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventions must be: new (novel), involve an inventive step (not obvious to a person skilled in the art, using problem-solution approach or other obviousness analyses), and be industrially applicable (capable of industrial production).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (newness) standard
rubrics_metrics.description: When a claimed invention lacks novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An invention lacks novelty if every feature or step in the claim is explicitly or implicitly disclosed within the relevant prior art, including inherent features known to a person skilled in the art. A single prior-art document defeats novelty if it contains all limitations of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step (non-obviousness) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: How inventive step is assessed following novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that are novel are then assessed for inventive step. Lack of inventive step is found where claimed features, though novel, would have been obvious to a person skilled in the art in light of common general knowledge. Obviousness can be based on a single source or a combination (mosaic) of documents; the 'problem-solution approach' is noted as an analytical method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes of substantive examination — notifications and reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms and notifications issued as results of substantive examination for patents and utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 18: notification of non-compliance with substantive requirements and invitation to submit observations and/or amended application; Form 21: notification of decision to grant patent/register utility model. Both Form 18 & Form 21 are accompanied by search and substantive examination reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant/registration and publication procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Steps and conditions leading to grant/registration and publication of patents and utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After issuance of Form 21, and after expiry of six (6) months and subject to payment of grant/registration and publication fees, the Office grants the patent/registers the utility model and publishes it. Form 25 is issued (presumably as formal record).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-establishment of rights (Sec. 5bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions for re-establishment of rights when timelines were missed through 'all due care'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed within 1 year from date of expiration of the time limit. The request is not deemed filed until the limitation fee has been paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendment (Sec. 5ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for amending patents after grant/registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed with the ARIPO Office in writing; not deemed filed until the limitation fee is paid. Any amendment to the claims must fall within the scope of the claims before the amendment.
